# No guide shows how to build a kanban board on your own records

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context

Engine 14 (cut on Nov 23, `ROADMAP.md` row 5) adds a board: `Neo.board.Container` shows the records of one store as cards in columns and swimlanes. Epic #20874 asks for "a runnable example and a guide per family". The scheduler and the Gantt chart have their pages (`learn/guides/datahandling/Scheduler.md`, `Gantt.md`), and the timeline column has its open leaf, #21195. The board was out of scope for #21037 because it was not on `dev` yet. It landed on `dev` with #21206 at `825047c9ea`, which resolved #20875.

## The Problem

A developer, or a coding agent asked for "a kanban board for our tasks", finds the class and one example. Nothing says that the columns are a projection of the store, that a move is one `record.set()`, how swimlanes are switched on, or how code and agents move a card. Today that is learned from `examples/board/basic` (212 lines in three modules) and the JSDoc of each config.

## The Architectural Reality

All paths are on `dev` at `825047c9ea`.

- `src/board/Container.mjs`: `Neo.board.Container`, `ntype: 'board'`, extends `Neo.container.Base`. Its `store` holds the cards. `statusField` (`'status'`) picks a card's column, and `orderField` (`'order'`) ranks it inside the column. With `columns: null` (the default), the board derives one column per status in first-seen order. Each entry of an explicit `columns` array takes `status`, `title`, `wipLimit`, `collapsed`, `color`, `locked`, `maxRenderedCards`, `overscan` and `retainOffscreen`.
- Swimlanes: set `laneField`, optionally `lanes` (`{value, title, collapsed}`), and `emptyLaneTitle` (`'Unassigned'`).
- `src/board/CardModel.mjs`: the fields `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `lane`, `order`, `assignees`, `tags`, `progress`, `color` and `dueDate`.
- One writer: `moveCard({record | key | cardId, status, lane, index, beforeId, afterId, fields})` commits a move as one `record.set()`. Drag, the card editor and an agent on the Neural Link use it. Events: `cardMove`, `cardsMove`, `columnMove`, `cardActivate`, `selectionChange`.
- Interaction: `dragResortable` moves cards and `columnsResortable` reorders columns, both `true` by default and independent of each other. `cardItems` (default title, tags, progress, avatars) sets what a card shows. `Neo.board.CardEditor` opens when a card is activated. `Neo.board.SelectionModel` provides keyboard navigation and multi-selection.
- The example: `examples/board/basic`. Its view root's state provider holds one `MainStore` (a `Neo.data.Store` of `CardModel` records), and the board and a table both bind it.
- The pattern for a guide page: `learn/guides/datahandling/Scheduler.md`, which has frontmatter with `seoTitle` and `seoDescription` and then one `#` title, and its line in `learn/tree.json`.
- Design authority: n/a — calls no existing behavior wrong.

## The Fix

One page, `learn/guides/datahandling/Board.md`, and one line for it in `learn/tree.json` after the Gantt line of `guides/datahandling`. Eight sections, in this order:

1. What a board is here: columns are a projection of one store, and a move is one record change that every other view follows.
2. A minimal board: the smallest working config with a store and `columns`.
3. Columns: derived or explicit, WIP limits, collapsed and locked columns.
4. Swimlanes: `laneField`, `lanes` and the unassigned lane.
5. Moving cards: drag, the keyboard, and `moveCard` for code and agents.
6. What a card shows: `cardItems`, and the card editor.
7. Long columns: `maxRenderedCards` and `overscan`.
8. Where to go next: the example, and the scheduler and Gantt guides.

Between 150 and 300 lines. Every code block is taken from `examples/board/basic` or checked against it, so that it runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `learn/guides/datahandling/Board.md` exists with `seoTitle` and `seoDescription` frontmatter and the eight sections above.
- [ ] AC-2: every class, config, field and event the page names exists in `src/board` on the pull request's base. The pull request lists them with file and line.
- [ ] AC-3: the minimal board of section 2 runs. The pull request says how it was run and shows a screenshot.
- [ ] AC-4: `learn/tree.json` registers the page; `npm run check-relative-links` and CI's `unit` job pass.
- [ ] AC-5: the page links the example and names no ticket number.

## Out of Scope

The board in the cyberpunk, dark and light themes (#20879), the Workstation's board pane (#20884), server-backed loading (deferred on the roadmap), a second example, and any change under `src/`.

## Avoided Traps

- **A reference dump of every config.** The page teaches what a first board needs and leaves the rest to the API docs.
- **Code blocks that were never run.**
- **A hand-mapped array of cards.** The board projects the records of a store, and the page shows a store.

## Related

#20874 (parent), #20875 (the board family, merged), #21037 and #21038 (the scheduler and Gantt guides), #21195 (the timeline column guide), #20498 (the standard for examples and the learning section).
